newsitem.title: USA: Warm weather boosts Montana wheat seeding.
newsitem.headline: Warm weather boosts Montana wheat seeding.

text.p: Winter wheat seeding progress was excellent amid unseasonably warm weather during the week ended Sunday, according to the Montana Agricultural Statistics Service.

Winter wheat was 88 percent planted against 65 percent a week earlier, last year's 89 percent and the average of 79 percent. Wheat had emerged on 43 percent of the acreage, up from 16 a week earlier and nearly matching the 42 percent average pace.
The weather allowed for 6.7 days suitable for fieldwork, but most areas of the state were in need of rain.
Topsoil moisture was rated 14 percent very short, 49 percent short, 37 percent adequate and nil surplus.
The sugar beet harvest also made excellent progress, with 57 percent of acreage harvested against 25 percent a week earlier, 42 last year and 40 average.

Pasture and range feed condition fell slightly from the previous week, with eight percent rated very poor, 27 percent poor, 40 percent fair, 24 percent good and one percent excellent. By the weekend, 44 percent of the cattle and calves were moved off summer ranges. There were a few reports of calves weighing less than normal at this time.
